newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-NEWCOMBE DEFENDS PLAYERS IN DRINKING ROW.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NEWCOMBE DEFENDS PLAYERS IN DRINKING ROW.

text.p: Australia's Davis Cup captain John Newcombe defended singles star Pat Rafter on Monday after an admission that he went on court drunk during the weekend's quarter-final victory over the Czech Republic.
Rafter said he was drunk after a night of celebration when he arrived at Adelaide's Memorial Drive ground for his reverse singles match against David Rikl on Sunday.
"I was still drunk coming here this morning," Rafter told reporters after Sunday's match.
"I started sobering up halfway through the match -- I felt great in the third set," said Rafter, who beat Rikl in three sets in the "dead" rubber match.
Australia, who eventually won the tie 5-0, took an unassailable 3-0 lead after the doubles on Saturday, prompting a team celebration that night.
Newcombe was unhappy that Rafter, world ranked 43, had made his admission but defended the player's professionalism.
"It was not too smart of Pat to say those things," Newcombe told reporters on Monday. "But I feel the comments have been exaggerated."
Australia number one singles player Mark Philippoussis also said he was suffering a heavy hangover during his victory against Martin Damm on Sunday.
"They were just a few celebratory champagnes after the match and at dinner. They followed that up with dancing and a late night," Newcombe said.
"As you can see from the boys' professional attitude they both went out there and won and would not have been able if they were not fit and capable of playing.
"The matter has been blown out of proportion."
